page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: rhythms that repeat in a period of about
Biological rhythms are the activities of an
organism that repeat at regular intervals.
steps.why: Circadian is only one kind of biological rhythm, so the answer defines the larger term first and then fixes the period at 24 hours — that period IS the whole difference.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the 24 hours. Without the period the answer defines any rhythm, not a circadian one.
Writing that the rhythm lasts 24 hours. It REPEATS every 24 hours.
steps.memory_tip: Circa means about and diem means a day: circadian is the about-a-day rhythm.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with the period in it, then one line placing it inside biological rhythms.

steps.label: Example
lines: Ex: the sleep and wake cycle of man.
Ex: the daily opening and closing of the
steps.why: The example must itself take a day, so the sleep and wake cycle is the one to give — it shows the period without needing another sentence.
common_mistakes: Giving the migration of birds as the example. That is a yearly rhythm, not a circadian one.
steps.memory_tip: Ask of any example: does it come round once a day? If yes, it is circadian.
steps.margin_note: One example is enough. Name it and stop.

insider_note: Both marks turn on the number 24 — a definition without the period scores nothing, however well it is written.
